note: All lines are original to this project (no attribution needed). Categories: start, consistency, struggle, comeback, milestone, revision. Daily pick = deterministic from dayKey; milestone lines are shown on streak/progress milestones.

quotes.text: You don't need a perfect plan today. You need one problem and twenty honest minutes.
The sheet is long. Today's row is short. Open it.
Every engineer you admire once stared at a blank editor and typed the first line anyway.
Motivation is a visitor. A habit is a roommate. Make it move in.
Start with the smallest version of today: one subtopic, one dry run.
Your future self is already proud of whoever opens the editor first.
Don't wait to feel ready. Ready is built by doing the first rep badly.
A quiet morning, a fresh tab, one solid problem. That's the whole recipe.
Thirty small days beat one heroic weekend.
Streaks are just promises you keep to yourself, one day at a time.
Consistency is boring on purpose. That's why it works.
You're not behind. You're mid-rep. Keep going.
Showing up on a tired day counts double.
Compounding doesn't care about your mood, only your attendance.
Make the habit so small it's embarrassing to skip.
The graph rewards the days nobody clapped for.
Protect the daily slot like it's a meeting with your dream job.
Rhythm beats intensity. Find yours and defend it.
If it feels hard, that's the feeling of your brain building new roads.
Stuck for an hour? Good. You're at the exact edge where learning happens.
A wrong answer is a free lesson with your name on it.
Brute force first. Elegance is a second draft.
Dry-run it on paper. The bug is usually hiding in plain sight.
Confusion is just understanding that hasn't arrived yet.
Recursion looks like magic until you trace the call stack. Then it looks like patience.
Nobody remembers how long a solution took, only that you finished it.
Read the editorial after you've fought for it. Then the lesson sticks.
Hard problems are just easy problems wearing a trench coat.
Missed a day? The streak is a tool, not a verdict. Start again right now.
The best day to restart was yesterday. The second best is the next ten minutes.
A pause isn't a failure. Quitting is a decision, and you haven't made it.
Come back gently. One easy problem is a real comeback.
Your progress didn't vanish. It's waiting where you left it.
Rebuild the habit before you rebuild the speed.
Look at the board. Every green square was a decision you made.
You've done more than you think. Scroll up and count.
A new phase unlocked. The roadmap is working because you are.
Celebrate for a minute, then pick up the next problem.
A week of showing up is the start of an identity.
This is what discipline looks like: a calm line going up and to the right.
Revision is where a solved problem becomes a skill.
Forgetting is normal. Reviewing on schedule is the cure.
Re-solve it without peeking. That's the real test.
Ten minutes of revision today saves ten hours of panic before placements.
Explain the approach out loud. If you can teach it, you own it.
Pick the next row. Not the whole sheet. Just the next row.
Build in public with yourself: log the day, even the messy ones.
Time and space complexity are just honest bookkeeping. Keep the books.
Small, steady, unstoppable.
Open the editor. The rest of the day will thank you.
